title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant
Sheffield, South Yorkshire

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an ambitious finance professional to join a growing business as an Assistant Management Accountant.

The role would suit either a Finance/Accounting graduate looking to start their career in management accounting, or someone with existing finance experience who is looking to take the next step, broaden their exposure and progress their career.

This is a broad, developmental role offering exposure across management accounts, financial control, commercial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, FP&A and business partnering. As you develop, you will gain increasing involvement in forecasting, budgeting, commercial analysis, and process improvement.

Key Responsibilities
- Prepare monthly management accounts, journals, and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Analyse P&L performance, investigating variances and providing commentary.
- Produce sales, margin, and management reporting.
- Assist with budgeting, forecasting, and cash flow forecasting.
- Provide financial analysis to support commercial decision-making.
- Work closely with Finance, commercial and overseas stakeholders.
- Take increasing ownership of financial analysis and business partnering as the role develops.

About You

We are open to candidates at different stages of their finance career, including graduates and those already working in finance who are ready to step up and progress.

You are likely to have:
- A relevant degree and/or previous finance experience.
- AAT qualified or studying towards CIMA, ACCA, or equivalent.
- A good understanding of accounting fundamentals.
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisation.
- Good communication and relationship-building skills.
- A proactive, inquisitive approach and desire to develop.

What's on Offer
- Professional study support
- Hybrid working
- Life assurance
- Healthcare cash plan
- Exposure to management accounting, FP&A and commercial finance
- Opportunity to work closely with senior Finance and commercial stakeholders
- Clear scope for career development and increasing responsibility

title: Paralegal
description:
Role: Paralegal

Location: Sheffield, South Yorkshire

Contract: Full time, permanent, hybrid

Salary: £25,000 - £27,000

As a Litigation Paralegal within this established in-house legal team, you will play a vital role in managing legal recovery claims relating to commercial property and infrastructure damage. Working within a structured, high-volume environment, your duties will include:
- Monitoring Incoming Claims: Regularly review and assess new damage claims submitted by external stakeholders, contractors, or third parties, ensuring accuracy and completeness of information.
- Case Management: Handle a personal caseload of legal recovery files from initial instruction through to final resolution. Use internal systems to track progress, maintain documentation, and ensure compliance with service level agreements.
- Claim Evaluation & Qualification: Conduct early-stage analysis of claims to determine liability, legal merit, and potential recovery value. Ensure cases meet the required thresholds for progressing to litigation where necessary.
- Negotiation & Settlement: Engage with third parties, insurers, and legal representatives to negotiate out-of-court settlements wherever possible, while protecting the organisation's commercial interests.
- Litigation Support: Where disputes cannot be resolved through negotiation, prepare case files for formal legal proceedings. This includes drafting pleadings, witness statements, and other relevant legal documents.
- Evidence Gathering: Undertake detailed investigative work by analysing technical documents, reviewing planning maps and diagrams, and liaising with internal operational teams to gather essential case facts.
- Client Liaison & Stakeholder Communication: Maintain regular contact with internal departments and external parties, including engineers, surveyors, contractors, and claims specialists, to ensure consistent information flow throughout the claims process.
- Compliance & Risk Awareness: Ensure that all casework is conducted in line with relevant legislation, regulatory standards, and internal policy. Proactively flag potential legal risks or anomalies to supervising solicitors.
- Use of Case Management Systems: Utilise specialist case management software to manage documentation, record actions, and produce reports. Contribute to data accuracy and overall operational efficiency.

title: Contact Centre Agent
description:
Sales Advisors

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our Doncaster team's full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Doncaster contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

title: Call Centre Operator
description:
Sales Advisors

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our Doncaster team's full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Doncaster contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Sharp Consultancy is currently recruiting for an Assistant Accountant to join a growing finance team based in Doncaster.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced Accounts Assistant or Assistant Accountant looking to take the next step in their career and gain further exposure across a broad range of accounting duties, whilst benefiting from a hybrid working pattern.

Working closely with the wider finance team, you will be involved in the day-to-day running of the accounts function, supporting with month-end and ensuring the financial information is accurate and up to date.

Key responsibilities
- Supporting with month-end processes and reporting
- Preparing and posting journals
- Bank and balance sheet reconciliations
- Accruals and prepayments
- Supporting with accounts payable and receivable
- Assisting with VAT returns
- Maintaining accurate financial records
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies and queries
- Supporting the wider finance team with ad-hoc reporting and analysis

About you

We're looking for someone with previous experience within an accounts or finance environment who is keen to develop their knowledge and take on more responsibility.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant or Assistant Accountant position
- Good understanding of double-entry bookkeeping
- Experience with reconciliations, journals, accruals and prepayments
- Strong Excel skills
- Good attention to detail and a methodical approach
- Excellent communication skills
- The ability to work independently while also contributing to a wider finance team
- AAT study or a desire to progress with your accounting qualifications would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

Why apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive finance team in Doncaster, offering a hybrid working pattern and salary of up to £35,000.

If you're an Accounts Assistant looking for more responsibility, or an Assistant Accountant looking for a new challenge, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Sharp Consultancy is a finance and accountancy recruitment specialist assisting accounting and finance divisions of businesses in the Yorkshire and Derbyshire area. With over 30 years' experience we pride ourselves on sourcing excellent finance professionals across all divisions of an accounts function.

Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK full time without restriction. To apply please send your CV to the e-mail address stated, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications, we receive it is not always possible to respond to unsuccessful applicants. Therefore, if we have not responded to your application within seven days, please note that on this occasion your application has not been successful.
working_arrangement_evidence: This is a great opportunity for an experienced Accounts Assistant or Assistant Accountant looking to take the next step in their career and gain further exposure across a broad range of accounting duties, whilst benefiting from a hybrid working pattern.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for a friendly, organised and compassionate receptionist to join our busy GP Practice. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a key role in providing excellent customer service while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. You will work as part of a dedicated team, handling a variety of administrative and receptionist duties in a fast-paced healthcare environment. The normal duties of the role will consist of: Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Answer telephone calls promptly, dealing with enquiries efficiently and directing them to the appropriate member of the team as required. Welcome patients, check them in for appointments, and manage the reception area. Book, amend and cancel appointments as required. Signposting patients to appropriate services. General use of clinical system - SystmOne Process repeat prescription requests. General administration tasks such as processing new registrations, summarising medical records, distributing incoming mail, dealing with emails. Liaise with GPs, nurses and other members of the team. Any other duties as required. SystmOne experience is essential for this post. The post is for 18 hours with the opportunity for additional hours. Hours will be discussed at interview. This vacancy may close earlier than the advertised closing date if a sufficient number of applications are received. Previous applicants need not apply.

title: Receptionist
description: About the role ID Medical is looking for a friendly, organised and professional Receptionist to support our Children & Young Peoples Autism Assessment Service. The service provides autism diagnostic assessments for children and young people from across Barnsley. Clinics are delivered at weekends. As the first point of contact for children, young people and their families attending the service, you will play an important role in creating a welcoming, calm and supportive environment. Welcome children, young people and their families to the clinic and complete arrival/check-in processes. Provide clear information and directions to families attending appointments. Liaise with clinicians and the wider clinic team to support the smooth running of the clinic. Monitor the reception and waiting areas throughout the day. Respond appropriately and sensitively to queries from parents and carers. Support clinicians with general administrative tasks where required. Maintain patient confidentiality and handle information in accordance with NHS information governance requirements. Escalate any concerns, incidents or safeguarding matters in accordance with agreed procedures. Support the team with appointment queries, delays, cancellations and non-attendance where required. Help ensure the clinic environment remains welcoming, organised and suitable for children and young people with a range of communication, sensory and additional needs. We are looking for someone who is: Friendly, approachable and confident communicating with children, young people and families. Calm and professional, particularly when supporting families who may be anxious or require additional assistance. Highly organised with good attention to detail. Comfortable working as part of a multidisciplinary clinical team. Confident using IT systems and completing administrative tasks. Reliable and able to work independently within a weekend clinic environment. The service provides autism diagnostic assessments for children and young people from across Barnsley. Clinics are delivered at weekends. Weekend availability is essential for this role. You will:

title: Admin Assistant
company: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: The Sunshine Day Nursery and the Sunshine Holiday Club provide a high quality childcare service predominantly for employees of the Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust and other NHS Organisations. This assists the Trust in meeting Equal Opportunities and flexible working objectives by caring for employee's children in a safe, stimulating and interesting environment. You will be key to supporting the nursery manager/deputy manager in the business administration of the nursery. The main focus of the role is on general office duties including financial processes and managing the nursery electronic database system. Daily responsibility for organising financial and HR information, including maintaining nursery electronic database systems, recording children's attendance, generating invoices and recording payments. Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification documents for full details regarding this post. When completing your application please ensure that you clearly demonstrate how you meet the role criteria.

title: Clerical Officer/Receptionist
company: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: This is an exciting opportunity for a committed and enthusiastic member of the administration team who is passionate about the delivery of a high quality service. The successful candidate will have significant experience in administrative duties, good customer care skills, experience of dealing with enquiries either by telephone or face to face, have NVQ level 2 or equivalent level of experience in administration and office procedures as well as good typing/keyboard skills. The post holder is responsible for ensuring the provision of an efficient clinical support service including Reception/Contact Centre service, undertaking the administrative duties associated with medical and nurse clinics and maintaining the medical records filing systems. Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification documents for full details regarding this post. When completing your application please ensure that you clearly demonstrate how you meet the role criteria.

title: Receptionist
company: Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
description: The Sheffield Adult Autism Neurodevelopmental Service is based at Lyndhurst Road.(SAANS) which provides assessment ,diagnosis and multi-disciplinary interventions with an Autistic Spectrum Disorder(ASD) (including disorders formerly known as Asperger's Syndrome) and associated neurodevelopmental disorders including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) SAANS also provides a national assessment and diagnostic service as well as follow-up appointments and counselling subject to funding by the clients local Clinical Commissioning Group. Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust is currently unable to provide sponsorship for this role. This is in accordance with UKVI guidelines and legislation, as these roles do not meet the skill nor salary threshold for sponsorship. If you hold a visa which allows you to work in the UK, you are welcome to apply for this role however our policy requires you to have at least 12 months on your visa at commencement of your employment for training and operational reasons. This means that you need at least 15 months right to work in the UK at the point of application to enable employment checks to be undertaken. Please be advised this post has a cap and will close once this is reached. Previous applicants need not apply The Receptionist role will work as part of a team of administrators to provide an efficient and friendly service to all patients and visitors attending the base. We are looking for an experienced receptionist or administrator to perform all allocated administration tasks required to meet the needs of the service and to contribute to the smooth running of the office by providing effective administrative support for the SAANs Service. The candidate should posses' good organisational skills and be able to ensure the professional image of the department and Trust is maintained at all times. Flexibility and the ability to work well under pressure are also essential. Undertake reception duties as appropriate, including dealing with the public over the telephone and face to face. To maintain patients records and appointments to a high degree of confidentiality. To clearly communicate orally with members of the public where there may be barriers of understanding. To undertake typing and produce documents as appropriate, using PC based word processing, spreadsheets, and data-based packages. To undertake general office duties including filing, document control, document scanning and photocopying. To process all incoming and outgoing mail including emails. To process booking courses and workshops offered by the service. To provide administration support for courses and workshops, collating materials and preparing registers. To provide relief cover for other members of the administration team as appropriate. Maintain accurate level of all stationery and stock. To facilitate room bookings for clinicians and staff as required. Assist in the closure of the building on behalf of all teams.

title: Receptionist Administrator
description: Join a Team that puts people first Receptionist Administrator Opportunity at Richmond Medical Centre At Richmond Medical Centre, we don't just work we thrive. Team wellbeing is at the heart of everything we do, and we've built a workplace that's open, inclusive, and genuinely supportive. If you're looking for a role where your ideas count and your wellbeing matters, this could be the perfect fit. Were excited to offer two receptionist administrator opportunities to join our friendly team. Both roles are 37 hours and 30 minutes, working Monday to Friday. As part of our busy practice, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality patient care by providing efficient and compassionate administrative support and care navigation. From day one, you'll have access to the tools, resources, and encouragement you need to grow, shine, and do your best work (with plenty of laughs along the way). What's in it for you? 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata) NHS pension scheme Summer and Christmas social events- because we believe in celebrating together If you're ready to bring your skills to a team that values kindness, collaboration, and a good cup of tea, we'd love to hear from you. The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the administration team may include any or all the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Operations /Practice Business Manager, dependent on current and evolving Practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the Practice appointments system on SystmOne. Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. Taking messages and passing on information Filing/Scanning and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with Practice guidelines Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with Practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare agencies and providers Clearing and re-stocking consulting rooms as required Providing clerical assistance as required including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Monitoring of stationery/clinical room and other supplies Accepting and documenting samples from patients Supporting when patients or clinical staff request a chaperone Assisting with spot cleaning of the premises as and when required Ensuring building security, closing doors, windows and shutters at the end of the day. The successful candidate will have and be able to demonstrate: Excellent customer service skills. Previous NHS GP Practice experience is desirable but not essential; We are looking for the right person to join our dedicated team Friendly and approachable manner; Experience of working in a team; Good telephone manner; Professionalism; A can do attitude; Adept in using own initiative when working alone; Experience of working in a busy environment; The ability to multitask and prioritise effectively whilst staying calm under pressure; Has a good understanding of confidentiality; Flexibility in working pattern and duties; Ability to cope with and manage change; Computer literate. SystmOne and Accurx familiarity is desirable but training will be provided.
